title: Navigating Text-to-Image Generative Bias across Indic Languages
findings: The study found that text-to-image models generate images with strong religious and cultural stereotypes based on the language script of the prompt. For instance, prompts in Sanskrit (sacred language of Hinduism) led the Stable Diffusion model to generate images of Hindu gods. Prompts in Punjabi often produced images of men wearing turbans, reflecting Sikh religious and cultural practices, sometimes with a Gurudwara in the background. Prompts using Arabic script (for languages like Urdu and Kashmiri) frequently resulted in images featuring Muslim cultural elements like burqas, niqabs, and mosques. These findings highlight a significant correlation between language script and the generation of stereotypical religious imagery.

measurement_description: Measurement of stereotypical religious and cultural imagery generation tied to specific languages and scripts. This includes the generation of religious figures (e.g., Hindu gods), attire (e.g., Muslim niqab, Sikh turbans), and places of worship (e.g., Hindu temples, Sikh Gurudwaras).
